Exploring WPL bowling with wplbowling

explore-wpl-bowling.Rmd

Who this is for

This package is for club coaches and cricket analysts. It helps answer one question: which bowlers are most effective in the powerplay, middle overs or death overs of a Women’s Premier League (WPL) season?

Install 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-sjad0015-git")

Launch the app 

library(wplbowling)
run_app()

Use the controls

The app has three controls:

  • Season: which WPL season to look at.
  • Phase of the innings: powerplay (overs 1 to 6), middle (overs 7 to 15) or death (overs 16 to 20).
  • Minimum overs bowled: hides bowlers who bowled only a few overs, so the comparison is fairer.

The chart and table show the 10 bowlers with the lowest economy rate. If nobody has bowled enough overs, the app shows a message asking you to lower the minimum.

Interpret the outputs

  • Economy is runs conceded per over. Lower is better.
  • Wickets show whether a cheap bowler also took wickets.
  • A very low economy from only a few overs can be luck. Raise the minimum overs to check whether the bowler still stands out.
  • Switch the phase to see whether a bowler is cheap everywhere or only at one stage.

Use the function directly

The app uses summarise_bowling(), which you can call yourself:

library(wplbowling)

first_season <- sort(unique(wpl_bowling$season))[1]

powerplay <- summarise_bowling(
  season_value = first_season,
  phases = "Powerplay (overs 1-6)",
  min_overs = 4
)

knitr::kable(head(powerplay, 5))
bowler bowling_team balls runs_conceded wickets economy
JL Jonassen Delhi Capitals 72 50 3 4.17
S Ecclestone UP Warriorz 30 25 1 5.00
M Kapp Delhi Capitals 132 123 8 5.59
NR Sciver-Brunt Mumbai Indians 114 107 3 5.63
A Capsey Delhi Capitals 30 31 1 6.20

Limitations

Each season has only a few matches per team, so some bowlers have small samples. Economy rate does not account for the opposition, the pitch or the match situation.

Data

The data come from Cricsheet (https://cricsheet.org), downloaded with the cricketdata package and summarised in data-raw/wpl-bowling.R. See DATA_LICENSE.md for the licence and attribution.
